label: Tab Router

Turn on routing *Applies the saved rules and automatic unmatched sorting. Defaults already include GitHub/GitLab → Dev and YouTube → Watch; enabling routing can move tabs immediately. Pictures can remain enabled independently.*

Subgroup separator *Splits a group name into nesting levels. With the default, Work / Email / Gmail creates a group three levels deep -- real nested tab groups, never pinned. Include the spaces if you want them; '/' with no spaces works too.*

Nesting limit *Hard cap on how deep automatic filing goes, counting the top group as level one. Two gives domain plus one subgroup. A safety valve: with Unlimited the mod already refuses to build repeated back-and-forth nesting.*

Rules *One per line, or separated by semicolons. Left of the > is a comma separated list of domains, right of it is the group name. Subdomains match automatically, so github.com also catches gist.github.com. First match wins, so put narrower rules first. You do not have to write these by hand: open the Browser Console and run TabRouter.suggestRules() to generate a block from the tabs you already have open, or TabRouter.suggestRules({subdomains:true}) to get a nested Parent / Child rule per subdomain. It copies to your clipboard and moves nothing.*

Sort everything automatically *Derives the group name from the site itself, so a page from somewhere you have never been still gets filed without any rule existing for it. Rules still win where they match, so use them to override the automatic name. This is the switch that makes the mod work with no setup.*
Use subdomains as subgroups *docs.proton.me becomes a Docs subgroup nested inside Proton, rather than just Proton. www is ignored, since it is noise rather than a real subdomain.*
How many subdomain levels *How deep to nest for hosts like a.b.example.com. One level gives Example / B. Two gives Example / B / A. Most sites never need more than one.*

Use URL path as subgroups *Subdomains cannot split a site that separates sections by path. nexusmods.com/games/cyberpunk2077 has NO subdomain -- www is stripped -- so every game lands in one group no matter how deep subdomain nesting goes. This reads path segments instead. One level on that URL gives a Cyberpunk 2077 subgroup inside Nexusmods, since 'games' is filtered as a generic word.*

Site list mode *Controls URL path subgroups. In Every site except these mode, listed sites also skip automatic pictures even with routing off. Only these sites limits path subgroups; it does not limit pictures.*

options.label: Every site except the listed ones

label: Site list for paths and picture exclusions *Comma-separated domains; includes their subdomains. Used by Site list mode above. Every site except these also excludes listed sites from automatic pictures.*

Subgroup by creator (YouTube) *Resolve the verified channel through anonymous, container-partitioned oEmbed requests. Private windows start no requests and persist no new metadata. Channel identity stays separate from folder names. Pictures work independently of creator grouping. Cached metadata is bounded to 300 records; failed requests retry on activity after 10 minutes.*

Pictures on tabs and subgroups *YouTube tabs use verified channel avatars; Nexus game/mod/profile tabs use the associated square game thumbnail (cover optional). No Nexus author portraits. Tabs can show pictures with routing disabled, including pinned tabs and Essentials. Manual Zen icons win. Pictures require Groupflow. Anonymous requests use the tab container, stop after 15 seconds, and never run in private windows. Pictures reuse one bounded cache: 100 subjects, 64-pixel icons; optional banners share the cache. Failed lookups retry on activity after 10 minutes.*

Nexus game icon *Square thumbnail uses Nexus’s 80-pixel game icon. Cover crops the portrait artwork. Missing thumbnails fall back to covers; unavailable artwork keeps the previous picture. Manual icons win. Refresh automatic picture retries the preferred source.*

Nexus game banners *Optional game hero artwork behind existing folder/tab styling. Uses the same verified game association; no routing changes. Off starts no banner requests. V1 games without hero artwork retain the normal fill. Banners are cached at 384 pixels wide. Requires Groupflow; update Glassflow for layered tab styling.*

Banner opacity (%) *0–100; default 25. Changes artwork opacity only, below existing tint, sheen and rim. Text, controls and selection states retain their styling. Changes reuse cached artwork without downloading again.*

Extra path words to ignore *Comma separated, ADDED to a built-in list of generic route words (search, watch, videos, results, games, category and similar). Numeric segments and file names are always dropped.*

Domain, subdomain and path name aliases *key = Pretty Name, one per line or comma separated. Applies to generated domain/subdomain names, path segments and verified subjects; explicit aliases win over learned names. TabRouter.learned() lists learned names; TabRouter.forget('slug') or TabRouter.forget() removes them.*
Create groups that do not exist yet *Off means tabs are only moved into groups you already made by hand, and rules naming a missing group do nothing.*
Sorting

Order groups and subgroups *Applies to groups at every level, in every workspace, after each routing pass. Creation order uses a timestamp stamped on groups this mod creates; groups made by hand have none and sort first. Manual leaves your arrangement untouched.*

Loose tabs above subgroups *Inside a group, individual tabs sit on top and subgroups below them. A tab newly filed into the main group is lifted above the subgroups on the next pass. Works in every sort mode, including manual.*

Follow Zen routes and containers *Destination is resolved in strict order on every filing move. Workspace: a matching Zen Space Routing rule (the Add Route for Domain entries) wins, then the workspace already holding the group, then the current one. Container: the routed workspace's default, then whatever the tabs already in the destination group use, then the workspace default, then unchanged. New tabs follow Zen's container rule before the first response. For loaded tabs, a container change reopens the tab only after checking for history, forms, POST data and session storage; protected pages retain their container. Folder/workspace moves can happen while pages are loading. Off: tabs keep their container, like Zen's Move to Space menu.*
Leave alone
Tabs already in a group *The important one. On, routing only ever touches loose tabs, so anything you filed by hand stays put. Turn it off only if you want rules to override your own sorting.*

Re-file tabs that drifted *A link opened from a grouped tab inherits that group even when it goes somewhere unrelated, which is why a stray domain stays stuck in the group it was opened from. With this on, a tab whose group no longer matches where it belongs gets moved. Only applies when tabs already in a group are otherwise skipped.*
Essentials *Essentials are pinned deliberately and are not loose tabs.*
Pinned tabs *Separate from Essentials.*
Timing
Sort everything at startup *Runs one pass a few seconds after the window opens. Off by default, since a session restore moving dozens of tabs at once is jarring.*
Wait before re-sorting (milliseconds) *How long after the last routed tab before groups are re-ordered. Lower is snappier; one pass covers a whole burst of tabs either way.*
Wait before the startup pass (milliseconds) *Only used when sorting at startup is on. Session restore needs a moment before tabs report real URLs.*
Troubleshooting

Log what it is doing *Prints to the Browser Console (Ctrl+Shift+J) under [TabRouter]. Also gives you TabRouter.preview(), which lists every tab with the group it would go to without moving anything, and TabRouter.sortAll() to run one pass on demand.*
